documents.title: Lab Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Outside psychiatry office called asking for a CBC, metabolic panel and UA before pt's appointment on 1/31; she'd rather draw here than at their lab. PCP okayed, orders entered, pt scheduled for a fasting-optional draw Wed AM.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, this morning's labs are normal: blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver tests, and the urine test. Hemoglobin is 13.2, which is a good number this far along. I've faxed a copy to your psychiatrist's office for the 31st.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry
Date of service: 01/31/2024

Re: Leah Martel, DOB 06/17/1990

Dear Doctor,

Leah returned for follow-up of major depressive disorder. She is now 36 weeks pregnant with her first child. Her depression has stayed in a reasonable place on sertraline 50 mg.

The main topic was abdominal pain she has had for about six months: a steady, dull ache spread across the abdomen that does not radiate and has no link to food or activity. She has been evaluated twice in the emergency department, had a normal abdominal ultrasound and saw gastroenterology, with nothing found. She describes a great deal of worry about her health, checks her body frequently, and has missed several days of work for the pain.

Medical history also includes migraine without aura and restless legs syndrome, followed by you and neurology. Medications: sertraline 50 mg daily, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, sumatriptan 50 mg as needed, prenatal vitamin daily. No known drug allergies.

Vital signs were normal. On abdominal exam there was no tenderness, mass or organomegaly. Your labs of 01/10/2024 were reviewed: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000, normal electrolytes and liver tests, normal urinalysis.

Impression: Somatic symptom disorder, with persistent abdominal pain and disproportionate health anxiety; major depressive disorder, stable.

Plan: continue sertraline 50 mg daily, which is compatible with pregnancy and breastfeeding. We will meet monthly for psychotherapy-focused visits through the postpartum period. I'd suggest one consistent point of contact for the pain, which I think is you, with scheduled visits rather than urgent ones.

Thank you for sharing her care.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Outside Letter Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Psychiatry letter reviewed. New dx somatic symptom disorder. Agree with plan for scheduled PCP visits for the abdominal pain rather than urgent ones; will set her up for a regular check after delivery.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/20/2024  Discharged: 02/22/2024

Patient: Leah Martel, 33, G1P0 -> G1P1001
EDD 02/26/2024 by LMP consistent with first-trimester ultrasound. Admitted at 39w1d in spontaneous labor.

Prenatal course: uncomplicated. Normal anatomy survey. Tdap given 12/06/2023. Followed by her PCP and GI for chronic abdominal pain with negative evaluation; by psychiatry for depression and somatic symptom disorder; on pramipexole for restless legs.

Labor and delivery: spontaneous labor progressed normally. Epidural. Spontaneous vaginal delivery 02/20/2024 of a liveborn infant, Apgars 8 and 9, birth weight 3,390 g. Estimated blood loss 300 mL.

Postpartum course: uncomplicated. Afebrile, normal blood pressures, voiding, ambulating, pain controlled. Infant well, discharged with mother.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: sertraline 50 mg daily, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin daily, sumatriptan 50 mg as needed.

Follow-up: OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks; PCP and psychiatry as scheduled.

documents.title: Baby is here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Baby arrived yesterday morning! Everything went smoothly, we're both doing great. Going home tomorrow. Do I need to see you or just OB?

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to all of you! OB will see you at 6 weeks. I'd also like to see you in about a month to check in on mood and sleep. The front desk will call to set it up.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with the baby in the car seat, four weeks out from an uncomplicated vaginal delivery (discharge summary reviewed). On maternity leave until April break.

Sleep is broken but she's coping; husband is doing nights on the weekend. Mood 'tired, not sad.' PHQ-9 6, GAD-7 6, no thoughts of harm to self or baby. Seeing psychiatry monthly, staying on sertraline 50.

The belly ache is still there some days. We agreed on a standing plan: she keeps a short log and we go over it at scheduled visits instead of urgent trips in. She liked that.

Migraines have been quiet. RLS fine on pramipexole.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing, tired. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, uterus not palpable. Calves soft.

A/P
1. Postpartum, doing well. OB 6-week visit booked.
2. MDD and somatic symptom disorder: stable on sertraline, monthly psychiatry. Scheduled visits here.
3. Migraine, RLS stable. Refills current.
RTC 3 months or as needed.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting renewal of pramipexole 0.125 mg tab, take 1 nightly, #90. Last office visit 3/20/24. Pended to PCP. -- Approved x 1 year.

documents.title: Surprise
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So... I'm pregnant again. LMP was May 17. Not exactly the plan for the timing but we're happy. OB is seeing me in July. Same meds as last time, same plan? I didn't skip the prenatal this whole time so at least that's covered.

documents.title: RE: Surprise
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, same plan as last time: sertraline and the prenatal vitamin continue, review the pramipexole with OB at your first visit, and sumatriptan stays your rescue for migraines if Tylenol doesn't do it. Let me know how the first visit goes.

orders.reason: Fetal spina bifida with Chiari II findings

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics & Gynecology Prenatal Visit
Date of service: 09/20/2024

Leah Martel, 34, G2P1001 at 18w0d by LMP (05/17/2024).

Seen for a routine prenatal visit. She has no complaints and her prenatal care has been regular and uncomplicated to this point. Her prior pregnancy (delivered 02/2024) was uncomplicated with a healthy term infant.

History: migraine, depression, restless legs, somatic symptom disorder. Medications: sertraline 50 mg daily, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily, sumatriptan as needed. Allergies: none known. Nonsmoker, no alcohol.

Exam: normal. Uterine size appropriate for gestational age.

The maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein from her second-trimester screen returned elevated. Ultrasound was performed today for further evaluation: single fetus; the skull has a lemon-shaped contour and the cerebellum is curved in a banana shape. No other abnormality was identified.

Assessment: Intrauterine pregnancy at 18 weeks with findings of fetal open spina bifida with Chiari II malformation.

Plan: results reviewed with the patient and her husband. Urgent referral to maternal-fetal medicine for detailed ultrasound and counseling, scheduled 10/01. We will follow along closely.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Hard news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted you to hear it from me. The 18 week ultrasound showed the baby has spina bifida. We see the high-risk team on Oct 1. I'm okay-ish. Mostly I just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Hard news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, I'm so sorry. Thank you for telling me. You don't have to carry this alone; call or text me anytime, including this week, and let your psychiatrist know too. I'll be thinking of you on the 1st.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation
Date of service: 10/01/2024

Ms. Martel, 34, G2P1001 at 19w4d, was referred for detailed evaluation after an elevated MSAFP and ultrasound findings of fetal spina bifida with Chiari II malformation on 09/20.

Detailed ultrasound today: single fetus with no cardiac activity, confirmed by two examiners. Biometry consistent with the stated dates.

Impression: Intrauterine fetal demise at 19w4d (missed abortion) in a pregnancy with fetal open spina bifida and Chiari II malformation.

We discussed management options. She and her husband chose dilation and evacuation, scheduled for tomorrow with the gynecology team.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine

events.reason: Dilation and evacuation for missed abortion

conditions.label: Maternal care for fetal spina bifida with Chiari II malformation

documents.title: Operative Report: Dilation and Evacuation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of procedure: 10/02/2024

Preoperative diagnosis: missed abortion at 19w5d.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: cervical preparation and dilation and evacuation under ultrasound guidance.
Anesthesia: monitored anesthesia care with paracervical block.
Findings: products of conception consistent with dates; evacuation complete on ultrasound at the end of the procedure.
Estimated blood loss: 150 mL.
Complications: none.
Disposition: recovered without incident and discharged home the same day with a responsible adult. Bleeding and infection precautions reviewed. Follow-up in gynecology clinic in 2 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

Gynecology

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Leah after her message last night that the MFM ultrasound on 10/1 showed no heartbeat and she had a D&E yesterday. Physically sore, bleeding like a period, no fever. Emotionally 'in pieces' but safe; husband and her mom are with her. No SI. Has a psychiatry appointment moved up to next week. Taking the rest of the week off school; I'll do a note. Booked to see me 10/16. Told her to call any hour.

documents.title: Work Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Leah Martel is under my care and is unable to work from 10/01/2024 through 10/07/2024 for medical reasons. She may return 10/08/2024. Please contact the office with any questions.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after D&E for missed abortion at 19 weeks; that pregnancy had a spina bifida/Chiari II diagnosis at 18 weeks. MFM and op notes reviewed.

Bleeding tapered off a few days ago. No fever, pelvic pain or discharge. Gyn post-op visit went fine per patient.

Mood: grieving, which she names as such. Sleeping poorly some nights, crying, still getting to school and looking after the baby. PHQ-9 9, item 9 zero. Saw psychiatry last week; staying on sertraline 50 for now, more frequent visits there. Husband and her mother around a lot. Abdominal ache unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tearful at times, appropriate. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Pregnancy loss, recovering physically. Missed abortion resolved.
2. MDD with grief: PHQ-9 9. Continue sertraline, psychiatry following closely. Discussed warning signs and how to reach me.
3. Flu and updated COVID vaccines today.
Video check in December.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from home after the baby's bedtime. Two months after the loss. Says the hard days are spaced further apart now. Back to full teaching load. Seeing psychiatry every 2-3 weeks; sertraline 50 unchanged. PHQ-9 6. No SI.

Migraines a couple a month, sumatriptan works. RLS fine. Belly ache still comes and goes, she's logging it as we agreed and it isn't driving visits.

Exam limited to video: well appearing, speech normal, affect appropriate.

A/P: MDD with grief, improving. Continue current plan. Annual physical in February.
